units.source_text: 陆士衡《豪士赋》中有句云：“落叶俟微飙以陨，而风之力盖寡。

en.t: In Lu Shiheng's Rhapsody on Eminent Men there is a line that says: Fallen leaves wait for a faint breeze to drop, yet the force of the wind is slight.

units.source_text: 孟尝遭雍门而泣，琴之感以末。

en.t: When Lord Mengchang met Yongmen he wept, but the feeling stirred by the qin was only a secondary cause.

units.source_text: 何者，欲陨之叶，无所假烈风；将坠之泣，不足繁哀响也。”

en.t: Why is this so? A leaf already about to fall has no need to borrow a violent wind; tears already about to drop do not require an abundance of mournful sounds.

units.source_text: 见《昭明文选》第四十六卷。

en.t: This appears in volume forty-six of the Zhaoming Wenxuan.
